claims.statement: A July 2026 primary preprint, revised 11 September 2026, reports differential microsecond-pulsed heat-capacity measurements of encapsulated CrSBr flakes from monolayer through bulk-like thickness under in-plane magnetic field, resolving layer- and field-dependent thermodynamic anomalies and estimating entropy with hBN and Debye-lattice background corrections.
assumptions: source-reported device calibration and differential reference subtraction
layer count and flake geometry as assigned in the source
magnetic-entropy interpretation uses source-selected hBN and Debye backgrounds and assumes an adequate spin/lattice decomposition
claims.status: source-reported v2 preprint result; interface reconstructed internally; raw data not replayed
claims.novelty_boundary: Bulk CrSBr heat capacity, field-dependent bulk heat capacity, magnetic anomalies, optical probes, transport, and a nanomechanical inferred heat-capacity signal predate this work. The bounded increment is direct pulsed calorimetry systematically applied across few-layer/monolayer CrSBr and low in-plane field.
costs: 50 microsecond 12-17 mA pulses with 100 ms off time
80-300 K temperature coverage and approximately 1e5 K/s local heating
approximately 1e-8 mbar vacuum and 1 mK base stability
hBN encapsulation and dry transfer under below 0.5 ppm oxygen/water
Pt R(T) calibration, differential electronics, AFM/optical flake geometry, and field calibration to plus/minus 2 mT
phonon and hBN background assumptions for absolute magnetic entropy
claims.falsifier: A matched empty-cell/hBN-only field sweep with a comparable anomaly, non-reversible H-H0-H measurements, or disappearance of layer/field trends after geometry- and strain-matched controls rejects the claimed magnetic interpretation or its transfer.
claims.next_gate: Obtain the deposited raw curves; replay heat-capacity extraction and compare field-paired, background-cancelled entropy against the Debye-subtracted result with H-H0-H drift controls.

claims.statement: If the same specimen/device has measured heat capacity C_obs(T,H)=A(T)+C_flake(T,H)+epsilon(T,H), where A is a field-invariant additive platform/encapsulant background, then integrating [C_obs(T,H)-C_obs(T,H0)]/T yields the total specimen entropy difference between H and H0 up to measurement and quadrature error; covariance propagates through the same trapezoid operator. This does not isolate spin-only entropy.
assumptions: same sample/device and matched temperature grid
platform and encapsulant addenda are field invariant or separately corrected
field-dependent sensor calibration, drift, and hysteresis are negligible or measured by controls
interpretation is total specimen entropy unless a validated spin/lattice decomposition is available
claims.status: derived exact conditional identity; synthetic finite-grid cancellation and Monte Carlo covariance checks; standard thermodynamics, not a novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: The identity is a standard subtraction/integration argument. Its practical output is total field-induced sample entropy without a Debye background; coupled field-dependent lattice entropy remains included, and absolute or spin-only entropy remains unidentified by this route.
costs: paired field sweeps on one flake
100 ms pulse spacing and full temperature sweeps
claims.falsifier: A field-dependent nonmagnetic-control curve comparable to the sample signal, or a paired entropy estimate not reproducible under H-H0-H ordering within propagated uncertainty, invalidates addenda cancellation or reproducibility. Spin-only attribution is independently unsubstantiated without a validated spin/lattice separation.
claims.next_gate: Apply the paired estimator and full covariance propagation to primary raw data; run H-H0-H bracketing and empty-cell/hBN-only field sweeps; retain total-specimen entropy terminology unless spin/lattice separation is validated.
